title: Kahal Kados Sheerit Israel: subscriptions to buy land and build a synagogue
citation: 15 Heshvan 5489
purpose: Buying a lot of land and building a synagogue for Congregation Shearith Israel, New York — the Mill Street synagogue, dedicated in 1730.
image_credit: Center for Jewish History
notes: Manuscript pledge list dated 15 Heshvan 5489 (autumn 1728). The signers undertook to pay half when the land was bought and half when building began. Benjamin Mendez Pacheco, Jacob Franks, Mordecai Gomez and (interlined) Moses Gomez were to manage the work and account for it, and give a £1,000 bond to Daniel Gomez, Abraham Isaacs and Nathan Levy on behalf of the congregation, to be recorded in the Town Clerk's office. The right-hand column is totalled £182 11s. 6d. (the entries as transcribed come to £181 11s. 6d.); Isaac Gonsales's £5 brings it to £187 11s. 6d., and later pledges were added on the left. Several names are torn or struck through.

title: Shearith Israel: memorandum of what we received of sundry people that signed on the other side
citation: Nov. 10
purpose: Payments received against the Mill Street synagogue pledges.
image_credit: Center for Jewish History
notes: Back of the pledge sheet, headed “Nov. 10” (year not legible). Running totals are written in: £56 6s., £71 10s., £87 6s. 8d., £100, £104, then Jacob Hays's £4 on 14 April. The right side lists payments made by Jacob Franks: to Mr. Nichols for drawing the writings (14s.), charges (9s.), Mr. Morison and Alderman Schuyler, a tax on the lot (2s. 10½d.), £100 to Mr. Cooper (presumably for the lot), and 18s. to Mr. Sharpas for recording — £103 5s. 10½d. in all, leaving £4 14s. 1½d. due to the synagogue. Upside down at the foot is the end of the agreement from the other side.

title: Subscription for the purpose of erecting a new synagogue at Canterbury

purpose: Building a new synagogue at Canterbury; the old one had been taken down to make the approaches to the South Eastern Railway, and the compensation was less than a quarter of the cost.
image_credit: Internet Archive (from microfilm)
notes: Republished subscription list to the Canterbury synagogue building fund, with the congregation’s thanks. Moses and Levy, Aldgate; Mr. Isaac Lyons, Duke-street, Aldgate; the editors of the Jewish Chronicle and the Voice of Jacob; and Mr. J. Jacobs, 29 Palace-street, Canterbury, secretary to the committee. A deputation was to visit London to solicit subscriptions. 74 entries totalling £404 1s. 6d. as transcribed; no total is printed. title: Appeal of Hirsch Edelman, printer and publisher of Königsberg: donations already received
citation: Vol. 3, no. 26
purpose: Support for Hirsch Edelman, whose Hebrew publications for the Jews of Russia were left on his hands by the Russian ukase restricting the import of Hebrew books.
image_credit: Internet Archive (from microfilm)
notes: Printed under the heading “Lost, on Tuesday last, an appeal, of which the following is a copy”; whoever found it was asked to bring it to 28 Bury-street, St. Mary-Axe. The appeal is signed Hirsch Edelman, printer and publisher, of Königsberg, September 5607, and cites the Chief Rabbi, Dr. Adler, as able to confirm his statements. image_credit: Internet Archive (from microfilm)
notes: Front-page appeal: donations fell far short of the previous year while distress had increased. A donor of five guineas could nominate one person to a permanent ticket for the season (two portions three times a week). Persons relieved in the week ending 8 February 1856: 2,650; since the start of the season, 17,600; total 20,250. 31 donations totalling £53 1s. as transcribed; no total is printed. Places and addresses are given only where printed; London street addresses are placed in London.

title: Metropolitan Free Hospital: donations and subscriptions announced at the anniversary festival
citation: Vol. VII, no. 28
purpose: Gratuitous relief of the sick poor of all nations, without letter of introduction, at 8 Devonshire Square, Bishopsgate Street.
image_credit: Internet Archive (from microfilm)
notes: Advertisement printed 16 April 1851. Gifts announced at the hospital’s anniversary festival at the London Tavern, Bishopsgate Street, on Wednesday 2 April 1851, David Salomons, Esq., Alderman, in the chair. Entries marked “a” in the list are annual subscriptions (entered with the role subscriber); the rest are donations. The notice addresses Jewish readers: a Hebrew visitor had said the hospital “might almost be called the Jews’ Hospital”, as it relieved about 5,000 cases a year among the Jewish poor, and the Committee appealed to “the wealthy members of the Hebrew persuasion”. A donation of ten guineas made the donor a Life Governor; an annual guinea, a Governor. 322 entries totalling £1,309 12s. 1d. as transcribed; no total is printed. Most donors are not Jewish.

title: Jews' Orphan Asylum: stewards of the anniversary dinner, 30 April 1851
citation: Vol. VII, no. 28
purpose: A dinner in aid of the funds of the Jews' Orphan Asylum (established 5591–1831), at the London Tavern, Bishopsgate Street, on Wednesday 30 April 1851, Frederick Peel, Esq., M.P., in the chair.
image_credit: Internet Archive (from microfilm)
notes: Advertisement for the dinner, listing its stewards. No amounts are printed: stewards usually gave or collected toward the dinner, but this list records only their names. Tickets were one guinea each, from the stewards, the London Tavern, or J. Dias, Hon. Sec., at the office of the asylum, Tenter Ground, Goodman's Fields. 60 stewards, including the president, vice-president and treasurer. The page image is shared with the Portsmouth list on the same page.

title: Melbourne Hebrew Congregation: special donations, Day of Atonement
title_original: Melbourne Hebrew Congregation. Day of Atonement.
purpose: Special donations to the Melbourne Hebrew Congregation on the Day of Atonement (25 September 1871).
image_credit: Newspapers.com
notes: “The Treasurer begs to acknowledge the following Special Donations”. Issue of 29 September 1871, p. 1 (from the clipping’s file name; it agrees with the St Kilda notice beside it, which announces services “This Evening” and “To-morrow (Sabbath and Succoth)”). Yom Kippur 5632 fell on 25 September. Names indented under “Mr.”, “Mrs.” etc. are printed without the title. 110 donations totalling £191 9s. 0d. as transcribed; no total is printed. The Treasurer asked readers to report errors or omissions and promised further lists.

title: St Kilda Hebrew Congregation: donations for a permanent place of worship and school-house
purpose: Establishing a permanent place of worship and school-house in St Kilda for the nearly 50 Jewish families living there.
image_credit: Newspapers.com
notes: The Committee stressed that members of the newly formed congregation did not intend to withdraw from the parent synagogues in Melbourne, and appealed to “their Metropolitan brethren”. 16 donations totalling £266 6s. as transcribed; no total is printed. A second list was promised. A sub-committee was appointed to collect and receive subscriptions.

title: New Synagogue, Sydney: first list of subscriptions
title_original: New Synagogue, Sydney. First List of Subscriptions.
purpose: Building a new synagogue in Sydney (the Great Synagogue, Elizabeth Street, consecrated 1878).
image_credit: Newspapers.com
notes: Printed total £3,219 13s. A fold in the page hides parts of the third to fifth lines; the names D. L. Levy, M. Levy and S. A. Anderson are partly legible, and their amounts are left blank because they cannot be read reliably. Earlier draft guesses of £250, £100 and £25 have been retained only in entry notes, not numeric totals. The printed total is preserved as source evidence; the transcribed sum is incomplete. “The Reverend A. B. Davis, £5 5s.” is printed as a heading line (the initial A is under the fold). Subscriptions were received by the joint honorary treasurers, S. A. Joseph and John Solomon, or by M. De Lissa, Hon. Sec., Synagogue Chambers, York-street, Sydney. Places are given only where printed; the rest are presumably Sydney.
